name: Bai Chay
tagline: The main tourist and hotel strip
description: The polished western heart of Ha Long, packed with hotels, the marina, beachfront promenade, Sun World, and the Queen cable car. This is where most visitors sleep, eat, and board cruises, with the densest cluster of comfortable air-conditioned cafes and tourist restaurants.
bestFor: First-time visitors and cruise-goers wanting convenience
pros: Walkable to marina and cruise departures
Most hotels, cafes, and English-friendly services
Beachfront promenade and Sun World nearby
cons: Quiet and thin outside peak season

name: Hon Gai
tagline: The local, working side with the market
description: Across the Bai Chay bridge, Hon Gai is the real, workaday Ha Long: the administrative and port core with a bustling central market, temples, and everyday local life. Seafood is cheaper and more authentic here, and prices for food and rentals run lower than the tourist strip.
bestFor: Budget stays and travelers wanting real local life
pros: Great local seafood and cha muc
cons: Less English and fewer tourist comforts

name: Tuan Chau Island
tagline: The marina and cruise departure point
description: A large developed island west of Bai Chay, connected by causeway, home to the main international marina where many bay cruises depart. It mixes resorts, a man-made beach, and entertainment complexes, feeling like a self-contained tourist enclave built around getting people onto the water.
bestFor: Cruise travelers wanting to be at the departure point

name: Cam Pha
description: East of Hon Gai, Cam Pha is a working coal and industrial town that serves as a quieter, cheaper gateway toward the eastern reaches of the bay and the Bai Tu Long area. Few tourists linger, but it offers low prices, local seafood, and a more off-the-radar base.
bestFor: Budget travelers heading toward Bai Tu Long Bay
pros: Very low cost and local pricing
cons: Very few nomad or tourist services
